terms.meaning: A word that means most ancient and also ever new, so everlasting.
"That which is heard": the Vedas, passed on from guru to pupil without a script.
"That which is remembered": post-Vedic works recalling the Vedas and Upanishads.
"The one who classified the Vedas": a name of the sage Krishnadwaipayana.
An auxiliary subject that helps in understanding the Vedas.
A school of Indian philosophy. The Darshanas are called its pillars.

items.name: Samhitha
items.formula: Mantras and hymns that praise natural elements and deities.
items.example: The first of each Veda's 4 divisions.

items.name: Aaranyaka
items.formula: Gives the meaning of the hymns and yagnas.

items.name: Upanishad
items.formula: Guru and pupil discuss creation, the creator and human existence.
items.example: The other three divisions stress karma; the Upanishads stress knowledge.

items.name: Prayer from the Brihadaaranyaka Upanishad
items.formula: Lead me from ignorance to truth, darkness to light, death to immortality.

groups.title: Smritis and the texts with them

items.name: Why Smritis are called Dharmasutras
items.formula: They give rules for everyday life and good conduct.
items.example: There are 18, and the Manusmriti is the oldest and most influential.

items.name: Which text guides our social outlook today
items.example: The hierarchy in the Manusmriti is not accepted today.

items.name: The six Vedangas
items.formula: Siksha (phonetics), Chandas (prosody), Vyakaran (grammar), Nirukta (etymology), Jyotishya (astrology), Kalpa (religious practices).
items.example: Together they help with pronouncing and practising the Vedas.

items.name: Itihasa and Puranas
items.formula: The epics are the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
items.example: There are 18 Puranas and as many Upapuranas, with stories of gods and kings' family lines.

items.name: The six major Darshanas
items.formula: Nyaya, Vaisesika, Saankhya, Yoga, Purva Mimamsa and Uttara Mimamsa.

items.name: Asthika and Nasthika
items.formula: Asthika accepts the authority of the Vedas; Nasthika does not.
items.example: Jainism, Buddhism and Charvaka are Nasthika.

items.name: Saguna and Nirguna
items.formula: Saguna has a name and form; Nirguna has neither.
items.example: Worship of named deities is already found in the Vedas.

items.name: Three schools of the Agama tradition
items.example: Agama literature made room for the worship of idols.

items.name: Swami Vivekananda at Chicago
items.formula: On 27 September 1893: "Help and not fight; assimilation and not destruction."
items.example: He spoke on the last day of the Parliament of Religions.

mistakes.text: Shruti is what was heard (the Vedas). Smriti is what is remembered (later works). Don't swap them.
Nasthika here means not accepting the authority of the Vedas. Jainism and Buddhism are in this group.
Four Vedas and also four divisions of each Veda: these are two different lists.
